name: Tata Consultancy Services Ltd.
business_summary: India's largest IT services firm (Tata group; Tata Sons holds 71.77%): ~600,000 employees (model knowledge), serving BFSI (~31%), consumer, manufacturing, tech and communications clients; North America ~50% of revenue, UK ~15%, Continental Europe ~15%, India ~5%. Q2 FY27: revenue Rs73,188 cr (+11.2% INR), US$7,642 mn (+0.2% q/q, +2.8% cc y/y - weakest September quarter in three years), operating margin 24.0%, PAT Rs13,884 cr, TCV US$9.6 bn, annualised AI revenue US$3.1 bn (>10% of revenue). Debt-free, dividend yield 2.6%. Mcap Rs9.02 lakh cr, P/E 16.5.

revenue_mix.segment: IT and consulting services (BFSI, retail, manufacturing, tech, comms, life sciences)
revenue_mix.geography: North America ~50% / UK ~15% / Europe ~15% / India ~5% / rest ~15% (model estimate)

exposures.mechanism: ~95% of revenue foreign currency, INR ~45% of costs (model knowledge); peers disclose ~25-30 bp margin per 1% INR. +3% => +80-90 bp on 24.0% EBIT = +3.5% EBIT; persistence 0.4 (hedges, wage resets), EV/MCap 0.95 => +1.3; set +1.5 consistent with INFY +1.5/HCLTECH +1.6. Empirical -1.18 (t=-0.9) wrong sign but insignificant: IT stocks rally on rupee strength via FPI flows (rupee +1.9% last month, stock +18.6% in a month).

evidence.note: Op margin 24.0% flat q/q, currency gains offset by investments

exposures.mechanism: +5% growth in US/EU enterprise IT services spend => TCS cc growth ~+2.5 pp (elasticity 0.5; ~50% North America, 15% UK, 15% Europe), operating leverage 1.4 => EBIT growth +3.5 pp for a year; at P/E 16.5 a sustained 2-3 yr step in growth is worth ~+4 to +6%; set +4.0. Q2 cc growth only +2.8% y/y (weakest Sept quarter in 3 years), so the lever is live.

evidence.note: USD revenue US$7,642 mn, +0.2% q/q, cc +0.5% q/q, +2.8% y/y; TCV US$9.6 bn
Reuters: weakest September-quarter growth in three years

exposures.mechanism: +1 = ~3% repricing of the services base from GenAI productivity pass-through; 3% x ~60% flow-through / 24% margin = -7.5% EBIT, persistence 0.5 => ~-3.5 to -4; offset: AI revenue US$3.1 bn annualised (>10% of revenue) and an 'anti-AI' relief rally in Oct (Nifty IT +16% in a month to 22 Oct). Consistent with INFY -5, HCLTECH -4, WIPRO -6, COFORGE -3.

evidence.note: Annualised AI revenue US$3.1 bn, >10% of revenue
Breakingviews: TCS AI strategy has key-man risk

exposures.mechanism: +1 = material tightening; US froze green-card filings for TCS (9 Oct) and a US$100,000 H-1B fee was blocked by court but appealed. Onsite visa cost +1.3-1.5 pp of revenue => -6% EBIT, ~50% passed to clients/local hiring, EV/MCap 0.95 => -3.

evidence.note: US froze green-card filings for TCS, Wipro, HCL, Cognizant, Microsoft

exposures.mechanism: Empirical +1.07 per +5% S&P (t=1.7, beta 0.82): US client sentiment and the AI trade move IT services; the Oct AI sell-off (22 Oct) hit the sector. Kept near empirical.
Empirical -0.41 per +5 VIX points (t=-1.1); defensive large-cap with beta 0.85.
P/E 16.5, dividend yield 2.6%: +25 bp on cost of equity => ~-0.9; debt-free so no funding channel. 10y G-sec ~7.4%.

US BFSI/consumer clients cut discretionary projects as the Fed funds rate rises (hike to 3.75-4.00% on 16 Sep; December hike odds 0.58); weight -0.7 per +25 bp via budget channel, cross-checked with INFY/HCLTECH -0.7.

evidence.note: Fed holds 3.75-4.00% with two hawkish dissents (event catalogue)

exposures.mechanism: UK and Continental Europe ~30% of revenue; +1 pp EU/UK demand growth => +1.0. India-UK CETA in force and India-EU FTA signing 16 Dec add optionality.

evidence.note: TCS Q2 fact sheet: UK/Europe all international markets grew q/q cc

exposures.mechanism: +2 pp wage inflation on employee cost ~56% of revenue = +1.1 pp of revenue = -4.7% EBIT, ~60% recovered via pricing/utilisation, persistence 0.5 => -1.8. Q2 margin already absorbed hiring and bench costs; wage hike cycle is a Q3-Q4 FY27 question.

evidence.note: Margin pressure from hiring, bench; senior staff to miss variable pay (Reuters 9 Oct headline)

supply_chain.counterparty: Large BFSI clients (e.g. UK/US banks, insurers)
